answer: Jittered handshake windows.** Identities gain standing only through low-rate, irregular liveness pings whose gaps are drawn from a hidden distribution; the network accepts a whisper-quiet node only if its timing matches. Clones must each mimic that jitter, so mass-registering N identities costs N independent timing profiles plus sustained background traffic, and any synchronized burst flags the karst of fake nodes for pruning. An oasis of genuine agents keeps its standing while attackers pay continuous per-identity maintenance.
